criteria.T: Compositional zero-shot learning (CZSL) aims to recognize novel combinations of previously observed objects and attributes. Prior work showed that large-scale vision-language models encode decomposable semantic structures that can be recomposed to enable generalization.
criteria.U: Multimodal retrieval-augmented generation over visually rich documents requires evidence at a finer granularity than entire pages. Existing visual retrievers typically index or return full pages, whereas training region-level retrievers often requires costly query-to-region annotations or noisy model-generated labels.
criteria.V: Backpropagation remains the dominant training paradigm, using backward gradients and local updates that can suffer from vanishing or exploding gradients in deep networks.
criteria.W: This paper addresses the problem of creating immersive volumetric videos from sparse and low-resolution capture resources. Conventional dense multi-view reconstruction methods can produce high-quality volumetric videos, but their reliance on costly capture setups makes them impractical in real-world scenarios.
criteria.X: Learning across medical imaging modalities requires making use of images without paired text and accommodating new domains while retaining existing representations. We propose a medical vision-language technique built around an expandable bank of modality experts.
criteria.Y: World models turn visual representations into predictions and actions. We argue that their visual foundation should combine physical-state information, native language alignment, and pixel reconstruction, so that a single representation can support prediction, instruction, and inspection.
criteria.Z: Text-to-Image models reproduce societal stereotypes, and existing mitigation applies one demographic correction to the whole scene. In multi-person scene generation this creates a trade-off: global steering improves aggregate balance only by homogenizing the people within an image.
criteria.AA: Understanding and modeling light transport in human-centric scenes is a longstanding challenge. While recent progress in diffusion models has boosted research in relighting, precise illumination control still lags, primarily due to the scarcity of diverse, high-quality, precisely labeled video relighting datasets.
criteria.AB: Recovering metric world-space hand motion from egocentric video supports understanding human interactions and transferring them to embodied agents.
criteria.AC: Cervical cytology presents a fundamentally ambiguous diagnostic landscape, where equivocal categories such as Atypical Squamous Cells of Undetermined Significance (ASC-US) occupy a morphological grey zone that is definitional.
criteria.AD: Autoregressive video diffusion models generate videos chunk by chunk, yet producing plausible continuations does not guarantee that they capture how scenes evolve.
criteria.AE: Visual accuracy, geometric validity, and agreement with applied forces are distinct requirements for visual dynamics. We introduce a diagnostic framework that connects reaction-free SI measurements to controlled interventions on coordinate readout, training integration, and actuator response.
criteria.AF: Single-image refocusing changes the focal plane and depth of field of a photograph after capture. It is inherently interactive: users try many focal points and blur strengths on one image, so each edit should be fast and change only the blur. Recent generative methods, however, rerun large diffusion models for every edit.

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We design and optimize a quantum error correction (QEC) decoder for NVIDIA GPUs, combining Relay belief propagation, a state-of-the-art message-passing algorithm, with order-zero ordered statistics post-processing. Our implementation uses CUDA Graphs to control GPU execution, stops updates for converged samples, and collects unresolved samples in queues for post-processing. We optimize sparse traversal through coalesced message accesses, prefetching, and register reuse, and accelerate binary post-processing with warp-level collectives. In addition, mixed FP16-FP32 arithmetic and INT8 quantization reduce message storage and traffic while retaining accuracy using accumulators at higher precision. We evaluate surface, hypergraph product, and bivariate bicycle code workloads on NVIDIA A100 and GH200 data-center GPUs and a commodity RTX 5080.

In which arXiv category (primary subject class) was this paper filed?

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Retrieval-augmented QA can fail even when the correct answer is in the retrieved evidence. This can happen when a competing answer satisfies some, but not all, of the question's requirements and is mentioned frequently in the retrieved documents, which can make it appear to be the best-supported answer. To test whether this retrieval skew actually affects the decision, we manipulate it directly: increasing the prevalence of passages that favor the competing answer makes the model more likely to select it. This points to a decision problem that candidate-level support alone cannot resolve. We therefore introduce Joint Constraint Aggregation (JCA), which compares candidates against the same question-derived requirements using the retrieved evidence.

In which arXiv category (primary subject class) was this paper filed?

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Weak-lensing magnification complements cosmic shear through its effects on galaxy fluxes, sizes, and number counts. We derive the optimal magnification statistics from galaxy properties and show that the optimal measurement can be decomposed into an optimal mean statistic and total number counts. The optimal mean statistic can be constructed from the residual distribution of a generalized fundamental plane (GFP), $F(i,\boldsymbol{X})$, which predicts galaxy size or, equivalently, flux from surface brightness $i$ and additional lensing-invariant properties $\boldsymbol{X}$. The function $F$ can take any form that reduces the intrinsic scatter and thereby improves magnification precision. For a Gaussian residual distribution, the optimal mean statistic reduces to the inverse-variance-weighted residual, or simply the residual for constant scatter.

In which arXiv category (primary subject class) was this paper filed?

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
In this work, building on previous studies of plane-parallel flows, we investigate the rapid growth of the frozen-in vorticity field in an axisymmetric poloidal flow. We present the results of numerical simulations performed using supercomputing resources. We show that exponentially growing velocity gradients can develop on the axis of symmetry, while vorticity gradients grow superexponentially. These results are qualitatively similar to those previously obtained for vorticity in a simpler two-dimensional flow.

In which arXiv category (primary subject class) was this paper filed?

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Generative AI can create programming feedback at scale, but validating its alignment with instructors' pedagogical goals and strategies remains challenging. Instructors may struggle to fully specify validation criteria upfront, as these often emerge through inspecting concrete examples and revising misaligned feedback. We present ValiAssist, a validation-by-demonstration system that infers reusable validation logic from instructors' revisions of AI-generated feedback and allows instructors to inspect and refine that logic as it is applied across other student submissions. In a comparative study with 16 instructors, ValiAssist helped instructors create and refine validation criteria, producing feedback that better aligned with their pedagogical intent (91% vs. 57%) and more than doubling the accuracy of correcting problematic criteria (77% vs. 32%).

In which arXiv category (primary subject class) was this paper filed?

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) offer scalable annotations of social and affective content, but their temporal agreement with human judgments and neural predictive value require further evaluation. We compared diffusion-based and autoregressive MLLMs with continuous human Theory of Mind (ToM) and affective valence ratings across three short cartoon movies. Behavioral analyses assessed temporally aligned Pearson correlations, rating distributions, and the effects of preceding scene descriptions. Ratings from each source were separately used in subject-specific regression models to predict regional fMRI responses. Model ratings captured aspects of human temporal variation despite systematic distributional differences, with generally stronger alignment for valence than ToM. Preceding context improved alignment in some conditions, depending on the model and movie.

In which arXiv category (primary subject class) was this paper filed?

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Recent world action models provide visual foresight and future prediction for robot manipulation, but lack explicit mechanisms for compositional skill reuse. Agentic robotics combines code-based planning and reasoning with reusable skills, but often lacks predictive grounding in physical dynamics. We introduce AW-0, an agentic world action model framework that integrates code-based planning with joint video and action prediction. We jointly model code, future video, and robot actions as three coupled generative streams within a unified mixture-of-transformers architecture. Within this architecture a code expert generates parameterized skill routines and control logic while video and action experts generate future visual states and low-level motor commands.

In which arXiv category (primary subject class) was this paper filed?

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Implicit neural representations (INRs) have been applied to deformable image registration, where a lightweight network maps a spatial coordinate to a deformation vector. Because an INR encodes one specific signal in its parameters, a fresh network must be optimized for every image pair at test time, which is slow. Existing methods reduce this cost by meta-learning an initialization across a population of image pairs, and condition the weights of the INR globally, so the same conditioning applies at every coordinate while the deformation field it initializes varies across the domain. We propose LUMINR, a meta-learning framework that accelerates this per-pair fitting and in which the conditioning is local instead.

In which arXiv category (primary subject class) was this paper filed?

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Symmetries play a crucial role in protecting the topological phases of insulators, ensuring the robustness of their surface states against perturbations. Traditionally, these symmetries have to be obeyed by the system as a whole, which is a rather strong constraint. In this work, we demonstrate that topological effects can also be realized through a substantially weaker form of symmetry that we coin \emph{partial latent symmetries}. For these, invariance is required only at certain energy scales of an effective Hamiltonian, rather than for the object as a whole. Applying this idea, we construct weak-symmetry versions of the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger and Benalcazar-Bernevig-Hughes models.

In which arXiv category (primary subject class) was this paper filed?

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
I discuss two important quantum optics experiments which depend on two particle interference. In the years since their first demonstration many interesting and instructive variants have appeared, including the use of atoms instead of photons as the interfering particles. This chapter gives a pedagogical overview of some of these results and argues that the two effects are closely related.

In which arXiv category (primary subject class) was this paper filed?

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
We give the first unconditional family of polynomial-time algorithms that breaks the $1/3$ approximation barrier for symmetric bimatrix games. For every fixed $δ>0$, an algorithm in this family computes a symmetric $(1-1/\sqrt{2}+δ)$-approximate Nash equilibrium, improving on the previous best guarantee of $(1/3+δ)$ due to Kontogiannis and Spirakis [2011].

In which arXiv category (primary subject class) was this paper filed?

Abstract of a paper posted to arXiv:
Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is an acquisition technique used for medical diagnosis. It is notably used for structural and functional MRI (or fMRI) image analysis. MRI data is known to be complex and noisy, so pipelines are created to extract and enhance relevant information in retrieved images. The NARPS study highlighted the significant variability that can emerge from different pipelines set up by independent teams while trying to answer the same research question about brain functioning. Having different implementations realizing the same task is a typical playground for software product lines (SPLs), which may be out of the sight of neuroimage practitioners. Thus, proposing an SPL out of these different pipelines falls back on a typical reverse-engineering problem with its usual difficulties.

Python Enhancement Proposal (Standards Track, created 03-Mar-2002)
Title: Enhanced Argument Tuples
Abstract: PyArg_ParseTuple is confronted with difficult memory management if an argument converter creates new memory. To deal with these cases, a specialized argument type is proposed.

What is the status of this proposal today?

Python Enhancement Proposal (Standards Track, created 01-May-2007)
Title: Introducing Roles
Abstract: Python's existing object model organizes objects according to their implementation. It is often desirable -- especially in duck typing-based language like Python -- to organize objects by the part they play in a larger system (their intent), rather than by how they fulfill that part (their implementation). This PEP introduces the concept of roles, a mechanism for organizing objects according to their intent rather than their implementation.

What is the status of this proposal today?

Python Enhancement Proposal (Standards Track, created 25-Oct-2016)
Title: Existence checking operators
Abstract: Inspired by 505 and the related discussions, this PEP proposes the addition of two new control flow operators to Python: * Existence-checking precondition ("exists-then"): expr1 ?then expr2 * Existence-checking fallback ("exists-else"): expr1 ?else expr2 as well as the following abbreviations for common existence checking expressions and statements: * Existence-checking attribute access: obj?.attr (for obj ?then obj.attr) * Existence-checking subscripting: obj?[expr] (for obj ?then obj[expr]) * Existence-checking assignment: value ?= expr (for value = value ?else expr) The common ? symbol in these new operator definitions indicates that they use a new "existence checking" protocol rather than the established truth-checking protocol used by if statements, while loops, comprehensions, generator expressions, conditional expressions, logical conjunction, and logical disjunction.

What is the status of this proposal today?

Python Enhancement Proposal (Standards Track, created 03-Jan-2001)
Title: Multi-dimensional Arrays
Abstract: This PEP proposes a redesign and re-implementation of the multi-dimensional array module, Numeric, to make it easier to add new features and functionality to the module. Aspects of Numeric 2 that will receive special attention are efficient access to arrays exceeding a gigabyte in size and composed of inhomogeneous data structures or records. The proposed design uses four Python classes: ArrayType, UFunc, Array, and ArrayView; and a low-level C-extension module, _ufunc, to handle the array operations efficiently. In addition, each array type has its own C-extension module which defines the coercion rules, operations, and methods for that type. This design enables new types, features, and functionality to be added in a modular fashion. The new version will introduce some incompatibilities with the current Numeric.

What is the status of this proposal today?

Title: Using site-packages on Windows
Abstract: The standard Python distribution includes a directory Lib/site-packages, which is used on Unix platforms to hold locally installed modules and packages. The site.py module distributed with Python includes support for locating other modules in the site-packages directory. This PEP proposes that the site-packages directory should be used on the Windows platform in a similar manner.

Python Enhancement Proposal (Standards Track, created 13-Oct-2011)
Title: General purpose decorator clause (aka "@in" clause)
Abstract: This PEP proposes the addition of a new @in decorator clause that makes it possible to override the name binding step of a function or class definition. The new clause accepts a single simple statement that can make a forward reference to decorated function or class definition. This new clause is designed to be used whenever a "one-shot" function or class is needed, and placing the function or class definition before the statement that uses it actually makes the code harder to read. It also avoids any name shadowing concerns by making sure the new name is visible only to the statement in the @in clause. This PEP is based heavily on many of the ideas in 3150 (Statement Local Namespaces) so some elements of the rationale will be familiar to readers of that PEP. Both PEPs remain deferred for the time being, primarily due to the lack of compelling real world use cases in either PEP.

Python Enhancement Proposal (Process, created 15-Mar-2001)
Title: Bug Fix Releases
Abstract: Python has historically had only a single fork of development, with releases having the combined purpose of adding new features and delivering bug fixes (these kinds of releases will be referred to as "major releases"). This PEP describes how to fork off maintenance, or bug fix, releases of old versions for the primary purpose of fixing bugs. This PEP is not, repeat NOT, a guarantee of the existence of bug fix releases; it only specifies a procedure to be followed if bug fix releases are desired by enough of the Python community willing to do the work.

Python Enhancement Proposal (Informational, created 14-Sep-2018)
Title: The External Council Governance Model
Abstract: This PEP proposes a new model of Python governance based on a Council of Auditors (CoA) tasked with making final decisions for the language. It differs from 8010 by specifically not proposing a central singular leader, and from 8011 by disallowing core committers from being council members. It describes the size and role of the council, how the initial group of council members will be chosen, any term limits of the council members, and how successors will be elected. It also spends significant time discussing the intended behaviour of this model. By design, many processes are not specified here but are left to the people involved. In order to select people who will make the best decisions, it is important for those involved to understand the expectations of the CoA but it is equally important to allow the CoA the freedom to adjust process requirements for varying circumstances.

Python Enhancement Proposal (Standards Track, created 02-Oct-2025)
Title: Explicit lazy imports
Abstract: This PEP introduces syntax for lazy imports as an explicit language feature: .. code-block:: python lazy import json lazy from json import dumps Lazy imports defer the loading and execution of a module until the first time the imported name is used, in contrast to 'normal' imports, which eagerly load and execute a module at the point of the import statement. By allowing developers to mark individual imports as lazy with explicit syntax, Python programs can reduce startup time, memory usage, and unnecessary work. This is particularly beneficial for command-line tools, test suites, and applications with large dependency graphs. This proposal preserves full backwards compatibility: normal import statements remain unchanged, and lazy imports are enabled only where explicitly requested.

Abstract: This memorandum describes RTP, the real-time transport protocol. RTP does not address resource reservation and does not guarantee quality-of- service for real-time services. The data transport is augmented by a control protocol (RTCP) to allow monitoring of the data delivery in a manner scalable to large multicast networks, and to provide minimal control and identification functionality.
